claims.statement: Tom Allen was born in Birmingham, England, in April 1840.
claims.excerpt: was born in Birmingham, England, in April, 184o.

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Waggoner of Birmingham in the autumn of 1861.
claims.excerpt: His first battle was with Waggoner, of Birmingham, $25 (45) a side, in the autumn of 1861,

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Young Gould for $100 (£20) a side about six months after his first fight.
claims.excerpt: Six months later he met Young Gould for g1oo (£20) a side, and the latter won.

claims.statement: Posh Price beat Tom Allen in fifty-five minutes in July 1862.
claims.excerpt: Posh Price whipped Allen in fifty-five minutes in July, 1862.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bingley Rose of Nottingham in ten rounds, lasting twenty-nine minutes, in January 1864 for $125 (£25) a side.
claims.excerpt: whom he conquered in ten rounds, lasting twenty-nine minutes, January, 1864.

claims.statement: Bob Smith, the 'Liverpool Black', beat Tom Allen in two hours and fifteen minutes about six months after the Rose fight.
claims.excerpt: Bob Smith, the “ Liverpool Black,” whipped Allen in two hours and fifteen minutes

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Jack Parkinson in twenty minutes for $125 (£25) a side.
claims.excerpt: whom he “cut into ribbons” in twenty minutes

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Posh Price fought forty-one rounds in November 1865; Price had himself arrested and the stakes went to Allen.
claims.excerpt: the two men fought forty-one rounds, lasting two hours and five minutes, in November, 1865.

claims.statement: Tom Allen defeated George Iles on 12 June 1866.
claims.excerpt: On June 12, 1866, Allen defeated George Iles

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought a 35-round draw with Joe Goss on 5 March 1867 in Monmouthshire, for $500 (£100) a side.
claims.excerpt: fought a draw with Joe Goss for $500 (£100) a side.

claims.statement: Tom Allen received forfeits of $250 (£50) each from Bill Thorpe, Peter Millard and Mike Cocklin.
claims.excerpt: received two forfeits of $250 (£50) each from Bill Thorpe, Peter Millard and Mike Cocklin.

claims.statement: Tom Allen came to America in July 1867.
claims.excerpt: Allen came to this country in July, 1867,

claims.statement: Tom Allen won his first American fight, a forty-three round bout with Bill Davis at Chateau Island, St. Louis, on 12 January 1869.
claims.excerpt: his first fight was with Bill Davis, at Chateau Island, St. Louis, January 12, 1869, when he won in forty-three rounds.

claims.statement: Charley Gallagher knocked Tom Allen out in the second round, after three minutes, on 23 February 1869 at Carroll Island near St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: and was knocked out by the latter in the second round, after fighting but three minutes.

claims.statement: Mike McCoole was given the decision over Tom Allen on 15 July 1869 on Foster's Island, after a crowd broke into the ring.
claims.excerpt: A crowd broke into the ring, and the referee gave the decision to McCoole.

claims.statement: The referee gave Charley Gallagher the decision over Tom Allen on 17 August 1869 at Foster's Island, though Allen had him beaten in the eleventh round.
claims.excerpt: although he had Gallagher whipped in the eleveuth round, after twenty-five minutes of sharp fighting, the referee decided in favor of the latter.

claims.statement: Jem Mace beat Tom Allen in ten rounds on 10 May 1870 at Kennerville near New Orleans, for $5,000 (£1,000) and the championship of the world.
claims.excerpt: he fought Jem Mace at Kennerville, near New Orleans, for $5,000 (£1,000) and the championship of the world.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was declared the winner over Mike McCoole after twenty-nine rounds on 23 September 1873 at Chateau Island, St. Louis, for $2,000 (£400).
claims.excerpt: St. Louis, Allen being declared the winner after twenty-nine rounds, lasting twenty minutes

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought a draw with Ben Hogan, the reformed preacher-pugilist, near Council Bluffs.
claims.excerpt: He afterwards fought a draw with Ben Hogan, the reformed preacher-pugilist, near Council Bluffs.

claims.statement: Joe Goss beat Tom Allen on a foul in 1876 in Kentucky, after twenty-one rounds, for the championship of America and $5,000 (£1,000).
claims.excerpt: His last fight was with Joe Goss for the championship of America and $5,000 (£1,000), in Kentucky, in 1876.

claims.statement: After the 1876 Goss fight Tom Allen was arrested and put under bonds.
claims.excerpt: Goss was declared the winner by a foul. Allen was arrested and put under bonds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen settled in St. Louis after his fighting career and was still living there in 1894.
claims.excerpt: He afterwards settled down in St. Louis, where he still lives.

fights.notes: 264 says there was no money at stake when Allen and Mace fought near New Orleans. Unclear whether these are the same bout.

fights.notes: 263 gives a 1871 title win over Bill McCoole on Chouteau Island, which this entry does not show.

fights.excerpt: He afterwards fought a draw with Ben Hogan, the reformed preacher-pugilist, near Council Bluffs.
fights.notes: Date not given; after the 1873 McCoole fight.

fights.excerpt: His last fight was with Joe Goss for the championship of America and $5,000 (£1,000), in Kentucky, in 1876.
fights.notes: Fought in two rings, one in Kent and one in Boone county. Goss was declared the winner by a foul. 263 says Allen lost the title on a foul.

notes: Portrait gallery entry, 1894, a career summary so all claims are retrospective. Dates and stakes are read from printed figures; the '(45)' and 'g1oo' OCR errors are read as £5 and $100. Conflicts with 263 (1871 title fight) and 264 (Mace stakes) are flagged in the fight notes.
